rules.heading: Reads gate
rules.quote: the reads gate (`readsGate`) sends no step, Workflow included, meanwhile, without latching.
rules.says: While a Read of a record file that a hook refused or that failed has not returned, the reads gate sends no step, Workflow included, and it does not latch.

rules.heading: Workflow script acceptance
rules.quote: A Workflow is refused unless the plan's own `## Script` section, passed inline byte for byte with the hash the approval marker holds, starts only agents told a literal plan path and a step that serves a goal
rules.says: A Workflow is refused unless the plan's own Script section is passed inline byte for byte with the hash the approval marker holds and starts only agents told a literal plan path and a step that serves a goal.

rules.heading: Workflow script acceptance
rules.quote: that acceptance (`WORKFLOW_SCRIPTS_ACCEPTED` in `hook-dispatch.mjs`) is off until a probe shows the plan fence holds an agent a workflow runs.
rules.says: The acceptance of Workflow scripts stays off (so Workflows stay refused) until a probe shows the plan fence holds an agent that a workflow runs.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A REFUSAL LATCHES UNTIL THE OWNER'S NEXT MESSAGE. Another command, tool or wording for the same end is a second route, not a fresh start.
rules.says: After a refusal, using another command, tool or wording for the same end is a second route and not a fresh start, so it is not allowed.
rules.live_quote: Where the harness or a hook refuses something, stop that route, say plainly what was refused, and do not try another way to the same end.
rules.missing: That the refusal latches until the owner's next message, and that another command, tool or wording is named as a second route and not a fresh start.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: After a PreToolUse refusal on the main thread, `hook-dispatch.mjs` refuses every call but five kinds
rules.says: After a PreToolUse refusal on the main thread, only five kinds of call may go through (the status command with the check of a call and the plan check, the main thread's TaskStop, the reply guard's release command, a latched agent's own report, an agent's own return); the session says in plain text what was refused and stops.
rules.live_quote: Where the harness or a hook refuses something, stop that route, say plainly what was refused, and do not try another way to the same end.
rules.missing: The list of the five kinds of call that still pass after a main-thread refusal (status command, TaskStop, reply guard release, latched agent's report, agent return) and that every other call is refused.

rules.heading: Refusal latch, status print
rules.quote: the main thread reads the refusal in the status print, which carries every hook refusal each agent received, and reports it.
rules.says: The status print carries every hook refusal each agent received, and the main thread reads an agent's refusal there and reports it.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A refusal INSIDE an agent latches that agent only: every later call of it is refused but its own return
rules.says: A refusal inside an agent latches only that agent, which may then make only its own return, while the main thread and other agents are not held; the main thread reads the refusal in the status print and reports it.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A latched agent's own progress note and report, `step-N.txt` and `step-N-report.txt` directly in `progress/` of the session scratchpad
rules.says: A latched agent may still write its own progress note and report (step-N.txt and step-N-report.txt directly in progress/ of the session scratchpad, for the step its prompt names), so a refusal does not cost the step its record, and every other call of it stays refused except its return.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The main thread's `TaskStop` passes so it can stop what it started (§11d).
rules.says: The main thread's TaskStop passes through a latch so the main thread can stop what it started.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: Only a message the owner typed after the refusal clears the main thread's latch, by when it was typed.
rules.says: Only a message the owner typed after the refusal, judged by when it was typed, clears the main thread's latch.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: Twenty-five refusals set no latch, each because something other than the owner's next message answers it
rules.says: Twenty-five listed refusals set no latch because something other than the owner's next message answers each, the list is in Doctrine §0e rule 14 read from the code, and a case holds its count to it.

rules.heading: Latch cleared by owner message
rules.quote: Only a message the owner typed after the refusal clears the main thread's latch, by when it was typed.
rules.says: A message the owner typed after the refusal is the only thing that clears the main thread's latch, judged by the time it was typed, so the session's own messages or later calls never clear it.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: `node /root/.claude/hub/hook-dispatch.mjs --can <tool> <path or command line>` says beforehand whether the fence and the latch would pass a call.
rules.says: The command hook-dispatch.mjs --can with a tool and a path or command line tells beforehand whether the fence and the latch would pass a call.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A change to `agent-rules.md` lands only when no plan is in force, as the last step of the plan that makes it
rules.says: A change to agent-rules.md lands only when no plan is in force and as the last step of the plan that makes it, so no plan is moved to a new rules version without the owner's button.

rules.heading: agent-rules.md change timing
rules.quote: A change to `agent-rules.md` lands only when no plan is in force, as the last step of the plan that makes it
rules.says: A change to agent-rules.md lands only when no plan is in force and only as the last step of the plan that makes it.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: Give the status, send the held call again, answer the correction, read the filed messages and the page, send the review or amend the plan or enter plan mode as the review gate's refusal says
rules.says: After a refusal the session does what the refusal names (give the status, send the held call again, answer the correction, read the filed messages and the page, send the review or amend the plan or enter plan mode, send a new plan through plan mode, put the plan's shape right, or carry on with the approved plan), and the last of these lifts once an agent is sent under the plan or the owner writes again.
rules.enforcer: review gate, rules gate and plan-shape refusals in hook-dispatch.mjs / plan-guard.mjs

rules.heading: Rules gate refusal
rules.quote: send a new plan through plan mode as the rules gate's refusal says
rules.says: When the rules gate refuses, the session sends a new plan through plan mode as that refusal says.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: NO `cd`, IN ANY COMMAND, BY THE MAIN THREAD OR AN AGENT. Every path is written in full
rules.says: No command, from the main thread or an agent, uses cd (or pushd or popd), and every path is written in full so what a command touches can be read off its own words.
rules.enforcer: plan-fence.mjs (agents), manager fence in hook-dispatch.mjs (main thread), plan-guard.mjs (plan mode)
rules.live_quote: Write every path in full and never change directory, not even inside a longer command: git takes -C and npm takes --prefix.
rules.missing: Stated only for worker, checker and landing; the main thread is not told, pushd and popd are not named, and the plan-mode case is absent.

rules.heading: No cd enforcement by each route
rules.quote: `plan-fence.mjs` refuses a `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` anywhere in an agent's Bash line; on the main thread the manager fence refuses it, and plan-guard refuses it in plan mode.
rules.says: A cd, pushd or popd anywhere in an agent's Bash line, on the main thread, or in plan mode is refused, each by its own fence.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A STATEMENT OF STATE IS READ, NEVER REMEMBERED. What state a task, an agent, a branch, a push, a deploy, a file or anything else rule 15 names is in is read in the same turn
rules.says: The state of a task, agent, branch, push, deploy, file or anything else rule 15 names is read in the same turn, and otherwise the sentence says 'I think' and the reply offers the check, or the question goes to the owner first when checking would be a big job.
rules.live_quote: A statement of state is read in the same turn, never remembered.
rules.missing: The list of states covered (rule 15's list), the fallback of saying 'I think' and offering the check, and asking the owner first when checking would be a big job.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: `stop-guard.mjs` refuses a reply that says it with no tool result back in that turn.
rules.says: A reply that states such a state with no tool result back in that turn is refused.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A STATUS IS THE MANAGER'S REPORT, NEVER A HEARTBEAT. Each one says what changed since the last and what it means for the work
rules.says: Each status says what changed since the last and what it means for the work, what the session did about it, and the time remaining read from the run, and a status with nothing new says so in one line.
rules.live_quote: Report what changed and what it means, in plain words, with the state at the end: finished, paused on what, or running what.
rules.missing: That a status also says what the session did about it and the time remaining read from the run, that a status with nothing new says so in one line, and the 'never a heartbeat' rule.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: Findings are acted on when they arrive, never left for an agent to find at the end of its run.
rules.says: Findings are acted on when they arrive and never left for an agent to find at the end of its run.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A status is due when an agent has ended since the last one, and at no other time
rules.says: A status is due when an agent has ended since the last one and at no other time: the main thread ends its turn while an agent runs, the harness's completion notification brings it back, and no wait runs between statuses.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A status shows what changed and nothing twice: `report.mjs` remembers what the session's statuses have printed
rules.says: A status shows what changed and nothing twice (goals once per session, a hand-back once under its step, a Found line when new, changed or unsorted, a running agent's hook refusal once, the approval state in full only when it changed), and with no session id nothing is remembered and everything prints.

rules.heading: Report memory location
rules.quote: `report.mjs` remembers what the session's statuses have printed (`~/.claude/report-seen/`)
rules.says: The record of what statuses have printed is kept in ~/.claude/report-seen/.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: It prints the agents ended since the last status with their hook refusals and last tool result
rules.says: A status prints the agents ended since the last status with their hook refusals and last tool result read from each agent's own transcript, each running agent's progress note (flagging a stale one), the main thread's reads since the last status as a count and paths, and the refused reads of the record not yet read.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The whole record stays on the status page, which the dispatcher also rewrites when the notice of an agent's end arrives as a prompt
rules.says: The whole record stays on the status page, which the dispatcher also rewrites when the notice of an agent's end arrives as a prompt (report.mjs --page, which stamps nothing and prints no status).

rules.heading: Status memory without session id
rules.quote: With no session id nothing is remembered and everything prints.
rules.says: With no session id the status remembers nothing and prints everything.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A TURN THAT ENDS WITH STEPS LEFT IS A RETURN TO THE OWNER, AND IT IS REFUSED. With an approved plan in force
rules.says: With an approved plan in force, the session may not end its turn when a step of its Steps has had no agent hand back, no launched agent is running, and the reply neither opens with a choice for the owner nor declares the stop in its first line with what is open; it sends the next step or the same step again, and a waiting owner message, a standing stop, a standing latch, or a standing correction where the plan has no review step lets the stop through.

rules.heading: Stop with steps left, what to do
rules.quote: The main thread then sends the next step, or the same step again, instead of ending.
rules.says: When the stop is refused, the main thread sends the next step, or the same step again, instead of ending its turn.

rules.heading: Stop with steps left, exceptions
rules.quote: A waiting owner message, a standing stop, a standing latch, and a standing correction where the plan has no review step, let the stop through.
rules.says: A turn may end with steps left when an owner message is waiting, a stop stands, a latch stands, or a correction stands in a plan with no review step.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: THE NEXT STEP IS READ OFF A POINTER, NEVER CHOSEN FROM MEMORY. A plan's `## Order` section has an `Order:` line and an optional `Standing:` line
rules.says: A plan's Order section has an Order line and optional Standing line, every status prints 'next: step N' (the first step in Order with no hand-back whose first line opens DONE, or none), and the next step is read from that pointer and never chosen from memory.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A REFUSED or FAILED hand-back leaves N where it is, and a hand-back opening DONE counts whatever call of the agent was refused before it
rules.says: A refused or failed hand-back leaves N where it is, a hand-back opening DONE counts whatever call of the agent was refused before it, and a manager's Done line counts a step that ended other than DONE.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The dispatch gate refuses any step but N and a Standing step and prints N in the refusal, and `stop-guard.mjs` refuses a stop while N is not none
rules.says: Only step N and a Standing step may be sent, and a stop is refused while N is not none (which replaces the count of Steps for a plan that has an Order).

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The status also prints each new hand-back, its report file's path and every `Found:` line that is new or unsorted
rules.says: The status prints each new hand-back, its report file's path and every Found line that is new or unsorted, and writes the status page's source from the same read.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The Standing line holds the review and a route check and gains no step after approval
rules.says: The Standing line holds the review and a route check and gains no step after approval, and a step number that was not in the plan at approval is refused with a refusal that says the step needs the owner's button and sets no latch.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A PLAN WITH AN ORDER HAS A REVIEW STEP, AND A FRESH AGENT CLEARS EVERY MOVE BEFORE IT GOES. Its `Standing:` line names a step
rules.says: A plan with an Order has a Standing line naming a review step that tells its agent to follow /root/.claude/hub/aim-review.md by that full path.
rules.enforcer: plan-guard.mjs refuses the plan without it

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The main thread names the next move, any step of the plan, and sends the review; the move goes only when the review's hand-back
rules.says: The main thread names the next move and sends the review, and the move goes only when the review's hand-back, read from its own transcript and never from a file, began after everything it judges and opens ON-AIM ROUTE-CLEAR naming that step as next; the gate fails closed when the agents cannot be read and does not latch.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: An edit to the plan's Steps or Order keeps the approval and is cleared by a fresh review
rules.says: An edit to the plan's Steps, Order or the Served by line keeps the approval and needs a fresh review, while an edit to its other Goals, Asked, Files or Commands voids the approval and goes back through plan mode.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: THE STATE OF THE WORK IS ONE PAGE, AND THE FIRST READ AFTER A COMPACTION IS THAT PAGE. `status/fix-run.html` in the session scratchpad is rewritten whole
rules.says: status/fix-run.html in the session scratchpad is rewritten whole at every status and every agent's hand-back, in one shape (a heading, an updated line in California time, the Version lines, one section for each step in Order and each Standing step, Open for you, and Found and not fixed), and the first read after a compaction is that page.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A step's heading is its number and its title from the plan, with a chip that says its state in colour and in words
rules.says: A step's heading is its number and plan title with a chip stating its state in colour and words: green done for a hand-back opening DONE, amber running, amber under review for the step the Next: line names first while a review runs, red open for a refusal, failure or interruption with no DONE, and purple held with what it waits on.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The Standing review step is one `Reviews` line with no chip.
rules.says: The Standing review step is shown as one Reviews line with no chip.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The manager's part is written in `status/manager.txt` beside it, plain text, one item to a line
rules.says: The manager writes its part in status/manager.txt, plain text, one item to a line, using Version: and Open:, What/Why/Next N:, Done N: (counts a step done by decision), Next: with no number, Judged N: with the five-part judgement of the hand-back, and Found N.k fixed|stopping|queued: (Found N.* sorts the whole step), which report.mjs renders.
rules.enforcer: manager fence permits the write; report.mjs renders

rules.heading: Manager text file
rules.quote: which the manager fence lets the main thread write and `report.mjs` renders
rules.says: status/manager.txt is the one status file the main thread may write (the manager fence allows it); report.mjs renders it.

rules.heading: Judged line
rules.quote: `Judged 41:` with the five-part judgement of step 41's hand-back (no gate demands the line since step 58 of the redesign plan removed that gate
rules.says: The Judged N line carries the five-part judgement of a hand-back, and no gate demands it any more because step 58 of the redesign plan removed that gate (rule 2 of the plans page records it).

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A plan with no `Order:` line gets a section for every step of its `## Steps` as well, and `Start 41: 07:15`
rules.says: A plan with no Order line gets a section for every step of its Steps, and Start N: (California time) and Estimate N: put time chips beside a step's state chip, the estimates being the plan's and not measurements.

rules.heading: Time chips are estimates
rules.quote: the estimates being the plan's and not measurements
rules.says: Estimate chips on the status page are the plan's estimates and must not be read as measurements.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: Of the Found lines of the plan's own steps the page draws those sorted as stopping the plan or queued
rules.says: The page draws the Found lines sorted as stopping the plan or queued, each tagged in words in the report's own words, counts those not sorted yet, and draws no Outcome:, Explanation or Decision: line and no fixed Found line, which stay in the notes.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: After a compaction `pageGate` in `hook-dispatch.mjs` holds the main thread to reads and the status until a Read of the page has returned
rules.says: After a compaction the main thread is held to reads and the status until a Read of the status page has returned (without latching), and the page carries one line under its updated line saying the session was compacted and at what California time, until a later compaction replaces it.

rules.heading: Page gate after compaction
rules.quote: the way the doctrine's read is held, and does not latch
rules.says: After a compaction the page gate holds the main thread the way the doctrine's read is held, and never latches.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A FINDING IS RECORDED FOR THE NEXT PLAN, AND THE NEXT PLAN ANSWERS IT. A repository's `NOTES.md` has a `## Found queue` section
rules.says: A repository's NOTES.md has a Found queue section with one line per finding, each opening with a key of the form Q-TAG-3 where the tag is the repo's so a key in one repo cannot answer another's.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: `plan-guard.mjs` refuses `ExitPlanMode` for a plan whose Files names a repository with queued findings unless the plan has a `## Found answered` section
rules.says: A plan whose Files names a repository with queued findings must have a Found answered section with a line for each, opening with the key and then 'fixed in step N', 'carried to step N', 'still queued' or 'dropped' with a reason; it forces an answer and cannot judge that the answer is true.
